instagram_caption:
Christopher Nolan's first film cost about six thousand dollars. 🎞️

In 1998 he had a day job. Half of each pay cheque went on rent, he says, and the other half on 16mm film stock. So he shot Following on Saturdays, fourteen of them spread across a year, in black and white, with friends as the cast and himself behind the camera. Most of it is first takes. His producer was Emma Thomas, whom he had met in his first week at University College London.

Twenty years on he was known for avoiding computer graphics. For Tenet he crashed a real Boeing 747, found by chance in an aircraft boneyard in Victorville, California; it was, he said, more efficient than miniatures and visual effects. For Oppenheimer he staged the Trinity test without computer graphics at all.

In 2024 Oppenheimer won seven Oscars. Emma Thomas accepted Best Picture; Nolan thanked her as the producer of all their films and all their children.

And the man who will not fake an atom bomb has never used email. He owns no smartphone (he keeps a flip phone for travelling, he says). It gives him time to think.

Real plane or computer graphics? 👇
